findings.title: Orphan cleanup can recursively delete a bucket's contents
evidence: apps/worker/src/tasks/orphan-cleanup.ts:52-67 — isFolderEntry() treats null/absent `id` as a folder; isFolderLike() rejects trailing-slash/prefix paths
apps/worker/src/tasks/orphan-cleanup.ts:78-130 — listAllFiles() recurses folder-by-folder with pagination (LIST_PAGE_SIZE=100), a MAX_DEPTH=8 cap and fail-closed read errors
apps/worker/src/tasks/orphan-cleanup.ts:227-235 — any non-object path (root, no slash, folder-like) aborts the bucket instead of being passed to storage.remove()
apps/worker/src/__tests__/orphan-cleanup.test.ts:369-445 — regression tests for folder entry (null id), .emptyFolderPlaceholder, root path and a folder surfaced with a non-null id
findings.impact: The scheduled cleanup can no longer delete a whole bucket by passing a folder prefix to remove(); catastrophic storage-loss path is closed.
findings.recommendation: Keep the folder-aware recursion + unsafe-path abort; add the storage integration fixture (nested objects + true orphan) suggested in the previous run to prove remove() is only ever handed concrete keys.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: recursive paginated listing, folder-entry rejection and the unsafe-path abort are all present with dedicated tests (orphan-cleanup.test.ts:369-445). Node was unavailable, so the suite was read, not executed.

findings.title: Approved-membership RLS predicate reintroduced six times; pending/suspended members could access tenant data
evidence: scripts/check-rls-predicate.mjs:38,77,100 — guard scans every migration newer than BASELINE_VERSION=5302430 and fails on a raw status-unfiltered membership predicate
.github/actions/unit-tests/action.yml:59 — guard is wired into the shared unit-tests action used by test.yml and validate.yml
Python reimplementation of the guard regex over supabase/migrations (>5302430): 0 violations (node unavailable, so the script itself was not executed)

supabase/migrations/5302057_fix_bootstrap_rls_fk_indexes.sql:39-55 — notifications_insert_system_or_admin is still the live INSERT policy; its admin branch is `select 1 from public.memberships m ... where m.user_id = auth.uid() ... and r.key in ('super_admin','admin')` with no m.status='approved'
grep supabase/migrations for notifications policies: only 5302029 and 5302057 ever create/replace them — no later migration rewrites this policy
findings.impact: Residual write-injection path: a pending/suspended member holding an admin-role membership can insert notifications for other users in the org via the anon-key + JWT PostgREST path. No tenant data read is exposed by this residual, but the register's claim that all module policies use the approved-membership helper is not fully true.
findings.recommendation: Add a follow-up migration that rewrites notifications_insert_system_or_admin with public.user_has_role(organization_id, array['super_admin','admin']) (or an explicit m.status='approved' filter); consider raising the check-rls-predicate baseline once the historical policy set is clean.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: the guard is present and effective for new migrations (0 violations reproduced), but the pre-baseline notifications INSERT policy still carries the raw predicate without an approved filter and remains live.

findings.title: `retention` worker task performs unbounded deletes and reports success on partial failure
evidence: apps/worker/src/tasks/retention.ts:23,31 — BATCH_SIZE=1000 and MAX_BATCHES=200 bound each purge
apps/worker/src/tasks/retention.ts:58-84 — purgeInBatches() selects ids, deletes in chunks, reports real counts and marks truncation
apps/worker/src/tasks/retention.ts:104-115,156-165 — non-positive windows are refused; any sub-purge error returns { ok: false, error }
apps/worker/src/__tests__/retention.test.ts:83-124 — tests for invalid windows, bounded batches, honest failure and empty backlog
findings.impact: Mass-delete lock/latency risk and silent purge failure are both addressed.
findings.recommendation: Keep the bounded batching; close the remaining test gap on age-boundary behaviour (see the separate retention-boundary finding).
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: bounded batching, truncation reporting and honest {ok:false} are present with tests. Residual documented separately: the test mock ignores the age cutoff, so the fresh-vs-expired boundary is unproven.

findings.title: Soft-delete columns remain dead schema; DELETE endpoints hard-delete
evidence: supabase/migrations/5302432_drop_unused_soft_delete_columns.sql:1-31 — begin/commit migration drops deleted_at/deleted_by from tickets, projects and documents plus their indexes, citing DATA-P1-003
grep deleted_at|deleted_by in apps/, packages/ and supabase/migrations (excluding the two historical migrations and docs/audits): no live code or type references
packages/sdk/src/database.types.ts — regenerated without deleted_at (no hits)
docs/ROLLBACK_PROCEDURES.md:64-76 — documents the hard-delete product decision and that recovery is backup/PITR-based
findings.impact: Schema no longer advertises tombstone semantics the code never implemented; no false recoverability.
findings.recommendation: None required; keep the documented hard-delete contract in ROLLBACK_PROCEDURES.md aligned with the API.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: the columns were dropped in 5302432 (commit 925ec007, ancestor of this commit), no app/type references remain, and hard-delete semantics are documented. The previous run's 'still open at 9c0b88c' was stale.

findings.title: Blanket `anon` DML grant + default privileges make every future table anon-writable unless RLS happens to stop it
evidence: supabase/migrations/5302434_anon_privilege_least_privilege.sql:34-44 — revokes the default-privilege grants for tables and sequences from anon

supabase/migrations/5302434_anon_privilege_least_privilege.sql:46-72 — revokes the blanket per-table grant, then re-grants INSERT only on public_interactions, store_analytics_events and store_quotes plus SELECT on four public store catalog tables
supabase/migrations/5302434_anon_privilege_least_privilege.sql:24,73 — migration is begin/commit wrapped
No migration after 5302434 creates a table and re-grants anon default DML (5302435/5302436 create no tables)
findings.impact: Least-privilege restored: future tables are deny-by-default for anon and the public surface is an explicit allowlist.
findings.recommendation: Keep the allowlist comment pattern; add a regression check that asserts information_schema.role_table_grants for anon matches the allowlist.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: 5302434 removes the blanket/default anon DML and keeps only the three INSERT + four SELECT grants; the migration is transaction-wrapped and no later migration reintroduces a default grant.

findings.title: Destructive table-replacement migrations are not transaction-wrapped
evidence: supabase/migrations/5302406_device_profiles.sql:3-7 — comment claims 'Idempotent... Safe to re-run', then `drop table if exists public.device_profiles cascade;` + `create table` with no begin/commit
supabase/migrations/5302407_network_diagrams.sql:8-15 — same pattern: 'Safe to re-run' comment, `drop table if exists network_diagrams;` + `create table`, no begin/commit
supabase/migrations/5302055_cleanup_dead_tables.sql:4-12 — nine `drop table ... cascade` statements (plus an FK swap) with no begin/commit
docs/migrations/naming-guide.md:168 — the repo's own standard: 'Use transactions - Wrap multi-statement migrations in BEGIN; ... COMMIT;'
tools/migration_chain_check.sh:102 — each migration is applied with `psql -f` (no --single-transaction), so a mid-file failure commits the drops and leaves the schema partially applied

supabase/migrations/5302110_restore_document_permissions.sql:1-10 — real precedent: 5302055's unwrapped `drop table ... cascade` silently destroyed can_read_document() and two documents policies and had to be forward-fixed
findings.impact: A failure between the drop and the create loses the old table's data and leaves the schema broken; the 'safe to re-run' comment is also misleading because re-applying the file on a populated database drops live rows.
findings.recommendation: Wrap every destructive migration in begin;/commit; (or rename/replace via create-new + transactional swap), archive data before drop, and correct the 'safe to re-run' comments; consider adding a static check that fails any migration containing `drop table`/`drop column` outside begin/commit.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: still open. 5302406:5, 5302407:13 and 5302055:4-12 remain unwrapped and unarchived; the repo's own naming guide and psql-based chain check make the failure mode concrete.

findings.title: `orphan-cleanup` deletes storage objects based on a truncated listing
evidence: apps/worker/src/tasks/orphan-cleanup.ts:6-10,97-127 — listAllFiles() pages with LIST_PAGE_SIZE=100 until a short page, so the listing is not truncated
apps/worker/src/tasks/orphan-cleanup.ts:119-123 — exceeding MAX_LISTED=10_000 aborts the bucket rather than acting on a partial view
apps/worker/src/__tests__/orphan-cleanup.test.ts:211-226 — 'pages through a bucket larger than one listing page'
findings.impact: The cleanup can no longer classify unlisted objects as orphans.
findings.recommendation: Keep the pagination + refusal semantics; add the real-storage integration fixture to prove no object outside the listing is removed.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: paginated recursive listing with a hard cap and abort semantics, covered by a pagination test.

findings.title: Migration CI dry-run diff is non-blocking; drift is never gated
evidence: .github/workflows/supabase-migrations.yml:90-125 — post-push `supabase db diff --linked --schema public`, ANSI stripped, fails with ::error on any alter/create/drop/comment/grant/revoke; allow_drift=1 downgrades to warning only via workflow_dispatch
.github/workflows/supabase-migrations.yml:68-83 — the dry-run plan is captured and uploaded as a 30-day artifact before the push
.github/workflows/supabase-migrations.yml:23-26,58-60 — migrations are serialized per branch and the Supabase CLI is pinned to 2.107.0
findings.impact: Unreconciled schema drift now blocks the migration workflow instead of being swallowed by `|| true`.
findings.recommendation: Keep the post-push diff gate; optionally add a required-review note when allow_drift=1 is used.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: the drift check runs after the push, strips ANSI, and fails closed; the only bypass is an explicit reviewed dispatch input.

findings.title: `audit_logs` org-delete cascade destroys compliance history; 365-day purge has no archive
evidence: supabase/migrations/5302108_fix_audit_logs_cascade.sql:2-7 — audit_logs.organization_id FK is `on delete cascade`
apps/worker/src/tasks/retention.ts:9-12,129-132 — audit_logs rows older than 365 days are deleted; no archive step
apps/api/src/routes/organizations.ts:397-419 — DELETE /organizations/:id hard-deletes the org, cascading away every audit row for it
grep archive|purge in apps/api/src and apps/worker/src: no audit archive sink exists (only storage/backup scripts mention archives)
findings.impact: Tenant offboarding and routine ageing both erase the compliance evidence trail; no cold-storage copy exists to reconstruct it.
findings.recommendation: Either change the FK to `on delete set null` (column is nullable) or write audit rows to an archive sink before org deletion and before the 365-day purge; record the retention/archive decision in the data-governance docs.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: cascade is unchanged (5302108) and the 365-day purge has no archive; the org DELETE route still hard-deletes. Previously carried unverified from 20261002.

findings.title: Several stores lack a retention policy and owner
evidence: Migration parse: 118 public tables define a created/captured timestamp; only three have purge code (audit_logs, notifications via apps/worker/src/tasks/retention.ts:129-134; public_interactions via 5302117 + apps/worker/src/tasks/public-interaction-retention.ts)

No purge exists for impersonation_log (5302133, cross-tenant access log), satisfaction_pulses (customer feedback text, 5302079), webhook_deliveries / webhook_dead_letters (request bodies, 5302032/5302050), document_shares (5302043) or business_os_snapshots (5302416)
supabase/migrations/5302071_governance.sql:54-75 — a retention_policies table exists, but apps/worker/src/tasks/retention.ts:9-12 hardcodes 365/90 days and never consults it
docs/MODULE_SPECS_GAP_AUDIT_2026-08-05.md:412 — independently documents that purge thresholds are hardcoded rather than driven by retention_policies rows
findings.impact: Unbounded growth of PII/audit-adjacent stores with no disposal owner; the product's retention_policies registry is not enforced by the only purge worker.
findings.recommendation: Publish a retention inventory (table → policy → owner → last exercised) and extend the retention task to the listed stores; either wire retention_policies into the worker or document why internal purges are hardcoded.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: still open. The set of unpurged timestamped stores is unchanged and the worker purge remains hardcoded. Previously carried unverified from 20261002.

findings.title: Generated DB types / schema can drift from migration intent
evidence: .github/actions/unit-tests/action.yml:47 — `node scripts/generate-db-types.js --check` runs in the shared unit-tests action (test.yml + validate.yml)
scripts/generate-db-types.js:570-588 — --check regenerates in memory and fails on any byte difference (line endings normalized)
scripts/generate-db-types.js:250-253 — DROP COLUMN is parsed (parseAlterTableDrop), which is why 5302432's dropped columns are absent from the types
packages/sdk/src/database.types.ts:2003,3229,1370 — types include file_request_uploads (5302430), network_diagrams and device_profiles; no deleted_at remains
findings.impact: SDK types track the migration corpus and CI blocks drift.
findings.recommendation: Keep the --check gate; add a spot-check test for exotic DDL if new syntax appears (e.g. rename column).
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: the generator handles CREATE TABLE/ADD COLUMN/DROP COLUMN and the --check gate is wired; types reflect the newest migrations and dropped columns. Node unavailable, so --check was reasoned from the generator + file contents, not executed.

findings.title: Orphan cleanup reference query is unbounded in the object list
evidence: apps/worker/src/tasks/orphan-cleanup.ts:26,169-184 — IN_CHUNK_SIZE=200; the documents/document_versions/file_request_uploads lookups are issued per chunk
apps/worker/src/__tests__/orphan-cleanup.test.ts:227-252 — 'chunks the reference lookup for large buckets (DATA-P2-002)'
apps/worker/src/tasks/orphan-cleanup.ts:155-212 — a failed reference read still aborts the bucket (fail-closed preserved)
findings.impact: Reference lookups no longer exceed PostgREST request limits, so the cleanup actually runs on large buckets without weakening fail-closed behaviour.
findings.recommendation: Keep chunking; no further action.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: chunked .in() with the fail-closed abort and a dedicated chunking test.

findings.title: Pre-baseline policies created without a preceding `drop policy if exists`
evidence: scripts/verify-rls.mjs:50,259-278 — rule 3 only enforces drop-pairing for migration prefixes >= 5302427

Python scan of pre-baseline migrations: 61 files create at least one policy with no same-file `drop policy if exists` (e.g. 5302032_webhook_endpoints.sql:11-13, 5302042_api_keys.sql:9-12, 5302034_ticket_comment_editing.sql:5-11)
Python scan of migrations > 5302427: every create policy is paired with an earlier drop (0 violations)
findings.impact: Only re-application/partial-apply safety of historical files; new migrations are already enforced.
findings.recommendation: Backfill drop-pairing into the affected historical files or document the exemption in docs/migrations; keep the 5302427 baseline.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: still open (informational). The pre-baseline exemption is unchanged and post-baseline files are clean. Previously carried unverified from 20261002.

findings.title: Migration version gaps undocumented; brief states 141 migrations, tree has 127
evidence: AGENTS.md:149 — declares 134 SQL migrations, latest 5302436; supabase/migrations contains 134 .sql files (count verified)
scripts/check-docs-counts.mjs:262-288 — fails CI when the AGENTS.md migration count or latest version drifts from the tree
grep for the gap versions (e.g. 5302084) in docs/: no rationale recorded
findings.impact: Counts are now self-consistent and CI-guarded; the remaining gap is forensic/documentation only.
findings.recommendation: Add a migration-history table to docs/migrations listing retired/skipped versions and the reason.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: the count/latest guard is fixed (134 = tree, CI-enforced), but the version gaps are still undocumented.

findings.title: `updated_at` is frozen on 69 module tables (no trigger; generic PATCH drops it)
evidence: grep `create trigger` across supabase/migrations: 17 statements total, all on the bootstrap core tables plus webhook_endpoints (5302032:22)

Migration parse: 69 tables define `updated_at timestamptz not null default now()` with no trigger, e.g. supabase/migrations/5302069_security_ops.sql:22,45,70,94; supabase/migrations/5302071_governance.sql:21,46,69,93; supabase/migrations/5302061_asset_tracker.sql:38

apps/api/src/routes/security-ops.ts:29-37 (PROTECTED_UPDATE_FIELDS includes updated_at) and :106-122 (PATCH never sets it); the same crudRoute pattern is used by governance.ts, field-services.ts, batch.ts and security-suite.ts
apps/api/src/routes/assets.ts:231,281-288 — PATCH increments version but never updated_at, so assets.updated_at stays at insert time
apps/api/src/routes/device-profiles.ts:126 and apps/api/src/routes/network-diagrams.ts:119 set updated_at manually — showing the inconsistency
findings.impact: Stale 'modified' timestamps silently break recently-updated sorting/filters, delta sync, cache invalidation and audit queries on most module tables.
findings.recommendation: Add one idempotent migration installing the existing public.set_updated_at() trigger on every public table with an updated_at column, or set updated_at centrally in the crudRoute factories; add a test asserting an update changes updated_at.
findings.note: new finding this run; the previous audit only noted 'few NOT NULLs / audit fields' as a scorecard gap. Concrete examples: offboarding_checklists, retention_policies, assets.

findings.title: Scheduled database dump and restore test target the dev environment only; production long-term backup is unproven
evidence: .github/workflows/db-backup.yml:12-14 — 'Backups target the dev database/buckets; the dev environment holds the SUPABASE_*/Spaces secrets these jobs resolve.' + `environment: dev`
.github/workflows/db-restore-test.yml:14 and .github/workflows/storage-backup.yml:30 — both also run in `environment: dev`
docs/RTO_RPO.md:10,18,24 — claims daily pg_dump to S3 with 30-day retention as the Postgres long-term recovery path
docs/ROLLBACK_PROCEDURES.md:114-118 — uses the S3 backup for data loss beyond the PITR window
grep infra/ for a production backup cron/job: none (only cloud-init/terraform, no backup unit)
findings.impact: Production recovery beyond Supabase PITR's 7-day window depends on an out-of-repo operator backup; the documented 30-day S3 recovery path and its freshness assertion (RESTORE_MAX_DATA_AGE_DAYS) exercise the dev database, not prod.
findings.recommendation: Run the dump/restore-test against a prod-scoped environment (or a prod DB URL secret) with the same baseline assertions, or explicitly document that S3 dumps cover dev only and correct RTO_RPO.md / ROLLBACK_PROCEDURES.md.
findings.note: new finding this run; overlaps the DR domain (DR-P1-003 covers encryption/offsite, not prod coverage). An operator-side schedule outside the repo cannot be ruled out from source.

findings.title: Retention purge boundary behaviour is untested; the mock ignores the age cutoff and the PII purge has no tests
evidence: apps/worker/src/__tests__/retention.test.ts:37-43 — `lt()` stores `api._cutoff` but `limit()` filters `(api._cutoff ? true : true)`, so fresh and expired rows are indistinguishable
apps/worker/src/__tests__/retention.test.ts:93-124 — tests assert batch counts and error propagation only; no fresh-vs-expired fixture
grep publicInteractionRetention|public-interaction-retention in apps/worker/src/__tests__/: no hits (the 90-day PII purge has no unit test)
findings.impact: An inverted comparison or off-by-one that deletes fresh data (the prompt's latent P0-class defect) would pass CI unnoticed.
findings.recommendation: Make the mock honour `.lt(col, cutoff)` and seed mixed fresh/expired rows on both sides of the boundary; add tests for public-interaction-retention (90d) with the same mixed fixtures.
findings.note: new finding this run; complements the verified DATA-P1-002 fix.

findings.title: Status-like text columns are not constrained by CHECK/enum, so app vocabulary is not enforced by the DB
evidence: Migration parse: 88 free-text status-like columns across module tables, e.g. supabase/migrations/5302069_security_ops.sql:20 (`status text not null default 'in_progress'`), supabase/migrations/5302061_asset_tracker.sql:15 (`status text not null default 'active'`), supabase/migrations/5302071_governance.sql:65 (`status text not null default 'active'`)

Only 15 named CHECK constraints exist repo-wide: six bounded numerics in supabase/migrations/5302103_add_check_constraints.sql:10-66 and nine version>=1 checks in supabase/migrations/5302113_add_check_constraints.sql:40-146

supabase/migrations/5302116_grant_table_privileges.sql:23-38 granted authenticated DML on every table and RLS policies admit approved members, so direct PostgREST writes can store arbitrary status strings
findings.impact: Values outside the app's Zod vocabulary can be persisted through the anon-key + JWT path, corrupting filters, reports and workflow state without a DB-level guard.
findings.recommendation: Add CHECK constraints or enum types per status vocabulary (or generate them from the Zod enums); prioritise the newest module tables and any status used for workflow routing.
findings.note: new finding this run; 'app assumptions not enforced by DB' special check. Impact is data integrity, not access control.

findings.title: No down-migrations and destructive migrations lack rollback notes despite the repo's own naming guide
evidence: docs/migrations/naming-guide.md:63,74,168 — requires rollback instructions/comments in the SQL file and BEGIN/COMMIT wrapping
grep rollback|revers across supabase/migrations: only 5/134 files mention it; none of the destructive files (5302055, 5302110, 5302116, 5302406, 5302407) do
docs/ROLLBACK_PROCEDURES.md:73 — schema recovery relies on reverse migration, PITR or S3 restore, but no reverse DDL is committed for these files
findings.impact: Incident recovery for schema changes is ad-hoc and reviewer-invisible; the repo's documented standard is not followed.
findings.recommendation: Add `-- Rollback:` blocks (re-create dropped tables/columns, re-grant) to destructive migrations and document the no-down-migration policy in docs/migrations.
findings.note: new finding this run; complements DATA-P2-002 (transaction wrapping).

findings.title: Generated DB types carry no commit/version binding
evidence: packages/sdk/src/database.types.ts:1-2 — header records only the generator and source glob ('Auto-generated from supabase/migrations/*.sql'), no commit/hash
scripts/generate-db-types.js:570-588 — --check compares regenerated content byte-for-byte; nothing binds the artifact to the revision that produced it
findings.impact: Low (CI enforces freshness) but consumers cannot tell which repository revision produced a shipped types file, contrary to the audit's artifact-binding rule.
findings.recommendation: Embed the migrations digest (or commit SHA) in the generated header and assert it in --check.
findings.note: new finding this run; hygiene/binding, not correctness.

report:
# Data, Schema, Migration, and Runtime Validation Audit

## Audit Metadata

- Audit name: repo-deep-dive (full hardening)
- Run: `mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8`
- Repository: `MaineCyberTech/mainecybertech`
- Branch: `main`
- Commit SHA: `8d299b8d`
- Generated at: 2026-10-11
- Auditor: repo-deep-dive subagent (base profile), domain 07
- Area code: DATA
- Output path: `docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8/07_data_schema_migration_runtime_validation.md`
- Scope limitations: static review only; no database connection, no Supabase CLI and no `node` in the audit environment, so repo guards were reimplemented/read rather than executed. Live row counts, lock timings and hosted-project state are unknown.

## Scope

Reviewed: `supabase/migrations/` (134 files), `supabase/seeds/`, `supabase/config.toml`, migration CI (`.github/workflows/supabase-migrations.yml`, `db-backup.yml`, `db-restore-test.yml`), migration tooling (`scripts/verify-rls.mjs`, `scripts/check-rls-predicate.mjs`, `scripts/generate-db-types.js`, `tools/migration_chain_check.sh`), DB-facing worker tasks (`retention.ts`, `orphan-cleanup.ts`, `public-interaction-retention.ts`), generated DB types, DB-facing API routes (org delete, generic crudRoute factories, optimistic locking, validators) and the rollback/backup docs.

Not reviewed in depth: live RLS behaviour against a running Postgres, migration lock timings on production-sized tables, the OpenAPI contract surface (domain 08), infra/DR runbooks in full (domains 12/13), and operator-side configuration that is not in the repository.

## Evidence Reviewed

| Evidence | Type | Why relevant | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `supabase/migrations/` (134 files) | SQL | Schema + migration safety | Version gaps: `5302026→5302028`, `5302038→5302041`, `5302043→5302050`, `5302083→5302085`, `5302135→5302402`, `5302428→5302430` |
| `supabase/migrations/5302055/5302406/5302407` | SQL | Destructive replacements | `drop table ... cascade` with no begin/commit |
| `supabase/migrations/5302108` | SQL | Audit cascade | `audit_logs.organization_id` `on delete cascade` |
| `supabase/migrations/5302432`, `5302434`, `5302435`, `5302436` | SQL | Latest fixes | Soft-delete removal, anon least privilege, RPC caller identity, admin-gate restore |
| `scripts/verify-rls.mjs`, `scripts/check-rls-predicate.mjs` | JS | RLS + predicate gates | Baselines `5302427` / `5302430`; wired via `.github/actions/unit-tests/action.yml:51,59` |
| `.github/workflows/supabase-migrations.yml` | CI | Apply + drift | Dry-run artifact; post-push `db diff` fails on DDL |
| `.github/workflows/db-backup.yml`, `db-restore-test.yml`, `storage-backup.yml` | CI | Backup/restore | All `environment: dev`; restore test asserts floors + freshness |
| `apps/worker/src/tasks/retention.ts`, `orphan-cleanup.ts`, `public-interaction-retention.ts` | TS | Destructive helpers | Batching, recursion, PII purge |
| `apps/api/src/routes/{organizations,assets,security-ops,governance,field-services,batch,security-suite,device-profiles,network-diagrams}.ts` | TS | DB-facing writes | Org delete, crudRoute PATCH, version preconditions, updated_at |
| `packages/sdk/src/database.types.ts`, `scripts/generate-db-types.js` | Generated TS / JS | Type drift gate | Types current; no commit binding |
| `docs/migrations/naming-guide.md`, `docs/ROLLBACK_PROCEDURES.md`, `docs/RTO_RPO.md` | Docs | Standards + recovery claims | BEGIN/COMMIT + rollback-comment standard; prod/dev backup mismatch |

## Verification Performed

Commands run (read-only) and observed results:

| Command | Observed result |
|---|---|
| `git log --oneline -3` / `git rev-parse 8d299b8d` | Target confirmed at `8d299b8d`; `9c0b88c` is its ancestor; `supabase/` unchanged between the two commits |
| `grep -c "begin;"` + per-file loop over `supabase/migrations/*.sql` | 47 files contain `begin;`; destructive files `5302055`, `5302406`, `5302407` do not |

## Executive Summary

The data domain has improved materially since the 20261004 run. All four headline fixes are present and effective at `8d299b8d`: orphan cleanup is folder-aware, paginated, chunked and fail-closed (`orphan-cleanup.ts`, tests at `orphan-cleanup.test.ts:369-445`); the retention task is batched, bounded and honest about failures (`retention.ts:23,31,58-84,156-165`); the dead soft-delete columns were dropped in `5302432` with the product decision documented; and the blanket `anon` DML grant was replaced by an explicit allowlist in `5302434`. RLS coverage is 134/134 live tables, the only policy-less table is explicitly deny-all, and the membership-predicate guard is wired into CI and clean for every migration after `5302430`.

The remaining risks are quieter. Destructive table replacements (`5302406`, `5302407`) and the nine-table cleanup (`5302055`) are still not transaction-wrapped — and `5302110` documents the real collateral damage a cascade drop already caused. `audit_logs` still cascades on org delete and is purged after 365 days with no archive. Only three of 118 timestamped tables have a retention purge. A newly found schema/runtime gap makes `updated_at` unreliable on 69 module tables: no trigger exists, and the generic PATCH factories explicitly strip `updated_at` without setting it. The scheduled database dump (and its restore test) run against the **dev** environment while `RTO_RPO.md` advertises 30-day S3 recovery, and production long-term dump coverage cannot be evidenced from the repo. Finally, the retention tests never exercise the age boundary — the mock ignores the cutoff — so a too-greedy purge would pass CI.

Recommended next actions: (1) wrap every `drop table`/`drop column` migration in `begin;…commit;` and archive before dropping; (2) install the existing `set_updated_at()` trigger on all 69 tables (or set it in the shared crudRoute factories); (3) settle the audit retention/archive decision (cascade vs set-null + cold storage); (4) extend the retention inventory to the listed PII/audit-adjacent stores; (5) fix the retention test mock to honour `.lt(col, cutoff)` and add mixed fresh/expired fixtures; (6) prove or document production backup coverage.

## Detailed Review

### Item: Migration safety (destructive DDL)

- Evidence: `5302406:3-7`, `5302407:8-15`, `5302055:4-12`, `docs/migrations/naming-guide.md:168`, `tools/migration_chain_check.sh:102`, `5302110:1-10`.
- What it does: replaces `device_profiles`/`network_diagrams` with `drop table ... cascade; create table` and drops nine "dead" tables; each file is a sequence of autocommitted statements when applied by `psql -f`.
- Missing controls: no `begin;/commit;`, no data archive, no static check that fails destructive DDL outside a transaction; the comments claim the files are "safe to re-run" although re-running drops live rows.
- Risks: partial-apply data loss; cascade collateral (already materialised once in `5302110`).
- Recommended improvement: wrap + archive + add a lint rule; correct the comments.

### Item: Audit-log lifecycle

- Evidence: `5302108:2-7` (cascade), `retention.ts:9-12,129-132` (365-day purge), `organizations.ts:397-419` (hard org delete), no archive code.
- What it does: destroys audit rows on org teardown and after one year.
- Missing controls: cold-storage archive or `on delete set null`; no operator-facing archive runbook.
- Risks: compliance evidence loss during offboarding and for aged incidents.

### Item: Retention framework

- Evidence: `retention.ts`, `public-interaction-retention.ts`, `5302117`, `5302071:54-75`.
- What it does: purges `audit_logs` (365d), `notifications` (90d) and `public_interactions` (90d, scheduled in `main.ts:71-79`).
- Missing controls: no purge for `impersonation_log`, `satisfaction_pulses`, `webhook_deliveries`, `webhook_dead_letters`, `document_shares`, `business_os_snapshots`; thresholds hardcoded rather than read from `retention_policies`.
- Risks: unbounded PII/audit-adjacent growth with no disposal owner.

### Item: updated_at audit field

- Evidence: 17 `create trigger` statements; 69 tables with `updated_at` and no trigger; `security-ops.ts:29-37,106-122`; `assets.ts:231,281-288`.
- What it does: new tables default `updated_at` to `now()` at insert; generic PATCH factories block client-supplied `updated_at` and never set it.
- Risks: stale modification timestamps for sorting, sync, cache invalidation and audit queries.

### Item: DB-facing runtime writes

- Evidence: 11 route files with `requireIfMatch`; 16 `.eq("version")` preconditions; no unfiltered `.update()`/`.delete()`; `parsePartialUpdate` mass-assignment guard (`lib/validators.ts:14-21`).
- Strengths: optimistic locking is enforced at the DB with version preconditions; mass assignment is closed for generic factories.
- Gaps: `notification_preferences`/`billing_customers` version columns are never used; status vocabularies not enforced at the DB.

### Item: Backup / rollback / drift

- Evidence: `supabase-migrations.yml:90-125` (drift fails), `db-restore-test.yml:135-210` (floors + freshness + RLS canary), `db-backup.yml:12-14` (dev), `RTO_RPO.md:10,18,24`.
- Strengths: drift gate, dry-run artifact, assertive restore test, encrypted/offsite-capable dump script.
- Gap: the scheduled dump and freshness assertion exercise the dev database; production long-term dump coverage is unproven in-repo.
